claims: SE derives the fixed-torus classical pressure endpoint and complete convex spectral budget, including repeated and zero spectral sets; these are not claimed as new classical theory.
SC proves a fixed-plane determinant identity and a quantitative L2 cone estimate without freezing the positive spectral block or requiring zero-mean amplitude.
The geometric-complement localization retains spectral and angular failure sets; a legitimate non-solenoidal cutoff removes the need for Leray nonlocal correction but not ordinary boundary cost.
A local L6 velocity estimate yields conditional suitable-weak regularity if the geometric-complement strain is L4 in time and L2 in space. The reference axis may measurably vary in time.
SC derives complete original-NS negative-eigenline/amplitude dynamics and a whole-ball amplitude-band angular estimate, with all stated derivative and pressure terms retained.
limitations: No new unconditional critical estimate, arbitrary-data regularity, singular solution, full Clay solution, worldwide novelty claim or human peer review.
The required geometric-complement L4 time norm is not proved from energy, which gives only L2. The full shape-gradient/eigenline-gradient mixed term remains uncontrolled by SE.
The angular Poincare estimate requires an entire ball with its specified amplitude band; it is not a theorem on arbitrary fragmented high-strain sets.
Smooth eigenline dynamics is only asserted on the one-negative/two-positive spectral open set; zero-spectrum contributions in SE are not removed.

The regularity endpoint uses a standard local regularity theorem with a primary-source hypothesis check for suitable weak solutions and, for a first smooth endpoint, matching extension and weak-strong uniqueness interfaces.

The unrelated broad convex-cone higher-integrability theorem is not imported; its perturbative hypotheses were checked. SE historical internal-checkpoint statements remain unchanged in this first combined SE-SC freeze.
